overview: Mayor Stephanie M. Burke held a press conference to provide updates on the city budget, zoning initiatives, ongoing capital projects, and municipal personnel changes. Key announcements included funding for new city staff positions, City Hall accessibility upgrades, a state grant for vocational school ADA improvements, and the appointment of Neil Osborne as Diversity Director.

items.title: Fiscal Year Budget Highlights
items.summary: Mayor Burke outlined key proposed budget additions, including a full-time recreation department, an opioid recovery coach, additional library staff, a traffic engineer, police technical support roles, and increased school maintenance funding.

items.title: Zoning Grants and Medford Square Updates
items.summary: Mayor Burke and Councilor Knight announced $40,000 in grant funding for a Mystic Avenue zoning review alongside ongoing zoning progress for Medford Square.

items.title: City Hall Renovations
items.summary: Mayor Burke detailed the renovation timeline for City Hall, which includes roof repairs, council chamber updates, and front entrance handicap accessibility improvements.

items.title: Senior Work-Off Tax Abatement Program
items.summary: Mayor Burke announced that applications are opening for the next round of the senior tax abatement work-off program starting in July.

items.title: Summer Recreation Programs
items.summary: Mayor Burke promoted the newly released summer recreation guide and a six-week youth park program scheduled for July.

items.title: Veterans Wall Dedication
items.summary: Mayor Burke announced a June 25 ceremony at Honor Roll Park in partnership with the Elks Club to dedicate new names on the Veterans Wall.

items.title: Diversity Director Transition and ADA Grant
items.summary: Retiring Diversity Director Diane McLeod announced a $130,000 state ADA grant for the vocational school, and Mayor Burke introduced Neil Osborne as her successor.
